text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government grounds Aviation Development Company, whose airliner crashed two weeks ago killing all 142 people on board.
- Compromise candidates may emerge for local council elections scheduled for next month, party leaders say.

- Federal government awards 4.7 billion naira contract to build a 132 kilowatt electricity line from Kano to Dutse in the north, says power and steel minister Bashir Dalhatu. Name of contractor unspecified.
- Twenty one persons including three chief executives of firms selling cars are charged with money laundering offences.
- Nigeria and visiting Commonwealth group end talks on suspension of the country from the group; both sides optimistic that there will be a truce in the hostility between them.
- Freed human rights activists return home.
- National electoral commission to register 52.1 million voters for elections leading to full democracy in 1998.

- Nigerian ambassador to the United States, business tycoon Hassan Adamu, worried that American investors are targeting other West African countries; launches campaign to stimulate investor interest in Nigeria's economy.
- Timely discovery of engine fault of Boeing 727 plane operated by Kabo Airlines averts another air mishap in Nigeria.
- Central Bank governor Paul Ogwuma predicts economic growth of between five and 7.5 percent next year in interview with the newspaper.
